title: Evaluation of Functional, Contrast-Free MRI as a Non-Invasive Biomarker for Renal Histopathological Changes
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate whether certain changes in the kidneys can be detected using an MRI scan without contrast agents. For this purpose, the MRI results will be compared with the findings from the kidney biopsy. In addition, medical information, such as blood and urine test results, will be taken into account. The study aims to determine whether kidney changes could in the future be detected or predicted without the need to take a tissue sample. In the long term, this could help reduce the need for kidney biopsies.
conditions: Patients who are scheduled to undergo a kidney biopsy for a medical indication will be included in the study.

interventions.name: Prospective, single-center, single-arm observational study evaluating functional, non-contrast-enhanced MRI as a non-invasive biomarker of renal histopathological changes by correlating MRI-derived parameters with histopathological findings from kidney biopsy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
written informed consent
voluntary participation
Exclusion criteria:
Claustrophobia
Artificial heart valve
Cardiac pacemaker
Cochlear implant
Any other metallic implants (fixed orthodontic braces, retainers, permanent acupuncture needles, broken biopsy needles, etc.)
Metal in the body (e.g., shrapnel)
Large-area tattoos, metallic makeup
Age under 18 years
Implanted drug pump
Severe cardiovascular disease, pulmonary or cardiac disease, diabetes
Neurological disorders, epilepsy, stroke, etc.
Hearing disorders, tinnitus, increased sensitivity to loud noises
Lack of written informed consent
Pregnancy (assessed using the standard MRI questionnaire of the Institute of Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology. Female participants who cannot clearly rule out pregnancy will be excluded from the study.)
Other MRI exclusion criteria (to be assessed by the study physician)
